reason: This is the only offered combination and should show how muscle responds to insulin.
expectation: I expect insulin to help muscle take up glucose from the blood, though the picture may show additional effects.

reaction: The before-and-after insets make the response clear, though it was expected.
reason: This is the only offered combination and advances the new between-meals goal.
expectation: I expect blood glucose to fall as cells continue using it and incoming glucose tapers, setting up a response to maintain its availability.

effect: Blood glucose has fallen between meals, while liver glycogen remains available; the pancreatic sensing cells are the next link.
reaction: The clock and vessel inset clearly establish the change, though it was expected.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it should show how the pancreas responds to falling glucose.
expectation: I expect pancreatic alpha cells to release glucagon, potentially signalling the liver to release glucose.

effect: Alpha cells release glucagon into the blood toward the liver, setting up the liver response.
reaction: The contrasting pancreatic responses are clear, though expected.
reason: This is the only offered combination and connects glucagon to the liver's stored glycogen.
expectation: I expect glucagon to signal the liver to break down glycogen and release glucose into the blood.

effect: The liver response completes the between-meals pathway: glycogen breakdown adds glucose to blood, and glucagon release then diminishes.
reaction: The sequential insets make the feedback loop clear, though the outcome was expected.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting glucagon to liver glycogen was most worthwhile: the planned sequence shows both glucose release and the subsequent reduction in the signal.

leastWorthwhile.text: Establishing the body with rising glucose felt like a predictable setup rather than a meaningful decision; it was the only offered combination.

surprise.text: Nothing was particularly surprising; the insulin and glucagon responses followed my expectations.

arbitrary.text: No action lacked a clear purpose, but each decision had only one offered combination, so compatibility was given rather than discovered.

continue.text: I would be unlikely to continue: the feedback connections are useful and clearly illustrated in the plans, but the single-option sequence offered little meaningful choice. The terms insulin and glucagon were shown through their actions rather than explicitly defined, which may leave some students wanting more explanation.
